builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
summary: LoopCache replaces fixed-position wave-style self-speculative drafting (WFD, LoopSpec) for Looped Transformers with confidence-guided dynamic draft updates across intermediate loops and a cyclic KV cache that restricts per-step memory traffic to one loop's cache. It costs implementation complexity: confidence-based switching logic, loop-cycle-aligned batching for verification, and selective independent KV caches for a few shallow layers. It can fail if the confidence-to-prediction-switch correlation does not hold on the target workload, if loop-sensitive layers require more independent caches than assumed, or if the model is not a Looped Transformer at all, in which case the method is inapplicable.
rationale: The technique applies only to Looped Transformers with loop-specific KV caches, an architecture the reader is unlikely to run in production, so it warrants monitoring rather than adoption.
technique: Confidence-guided self-speculative decoding with cyclic loop KV cache

claims.statement: LoopCache replaces fixed-position wave-style self-speculative drafting (WFD, LoopSpec) for Looped Transformers with confidence-guided dynamic draft updates across intermediate loops and a cyclic KV cache that restricts per-step memory traffic to one loop's cache. It costs implementation complexity: confidence-based switching logic, loop-cycle-aligned batching for verification, and selective independent KV caches for a few shallow layers. It can fail if the confidence-to-prediction-switch correlation does not hold on the target workload, if loop-sensitive layers require more independent caches than assumed, or if the model is not a Looped Transformer at all, in which case the method is inapplicable.
Average 10.25x speedup over WaveFront Decoding and 14.56x over LoopSpec on long-context Looped Transformers.
